title: Patch: a private lobby stays on screen when one refresh fails, instead of turning into an error card

# #4021: Patch: a private lobby stays on screen when one refresh fails, instead of turning into an error card
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
A private lobby is the room friends gather in before a 1v1, co-op or 2v2 game. It refreshes itself after every action, after every update from the server, and every few seconds while the live connection is down. If any one of those refreshes fails (a phone switching networks, a brief server hiccup), the whole lobby is swapped for “The lobby could not be read” and a Try again button. That throws away the deck the player had picked but not sent, the start countdown, and any message about a refused action. While the live connection is up nothing refreshes it again, so a member can sit on that card after the host has already started the game. Once built, a failed refresh keeps the lobby the player was looking at and tries again a few seconds later. The error card appears only when the lobby could never be read at all.

## Why
- `apps/web/src/lobby/LobbyScreen.tsx:120-131`: every failed read sets the read to `{ kind: 'failed' }`, whatever was on screen. That read runs on every push (`:138`), on every change of the socket (`:141-145`), every `LOBBY_POLL_MS` while the socket is down (`:148-154`), at the lobby's expiry (`:156-162`) and after every action (`run`'s `finally`, `:240-243`).
- `:194-201` then replaces the body with the error card. That unmounts `Lobby` and its local state: the action's refusal (`error`, `:220`), the picked deck (`pick`, `:715`), the invited marks (`sent`, `:855`) and the countdown's start (`seenAt`, `:914`).
- `attempt` (`apps/web/src/net/errors.ts:16`) does not retry.
- The repo's own polling hook does the opposite on purpose: `apps/web/src/together/session.ts:36` says “A failed read after a good one keeps the good one”.
- `LobbyScreen.test.tsx` covers a failure on the first read only.

## Proposal
1. In `useLobbyRead`'s failure handler, keep a ready read: `setRead((previous) => previous.kind === 'ready' ? previous : { kind: 'failed', message })`. A 404 still closes the lobby, as today.
2. After a failed re-read, schedule one more read after `LOBBY_POLL_MS`, whether the socket is up or not, so a start or a change still reaches the member.
3. Rejected alternative: a banner over the lobby saying the refresh failed. It adds surface for a blip the next read fixes, and the co-op hook already keeps the good read silently.

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/lobby/LobbyScreen.tsx` (`useLobbyRead`)
- `apps/web/src/lobby/LobbyScreen.test.tsx`
- No SPEC change: R3730000's reads are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test serves a lobby, picks a deck, makes the next lobby read fail with a network error and triggers a push. The lobby, its Leave button and the picked deck are still shown, and the text “could not be read” is absent. (Check the text, since the error testid also marks the inline refusal.)
- [ ] The same test lets the read succeed again and sees the lobby read once more within `LOBBY_POLL_MS` with the socket up.
- [ ] An action's refusal message survives a failed re-read after it.
- [ ] A failure on the first read still shows the error card, and a 404 still shows the lobby as closed.

## Size and risks
Very small: one hook and its tests. Medium difficulty. Low risk: a lobby shown a few seconds stale is the same trade the co-op screen already makes.
